title: Board and Drug Control Program Policy 2019-02 requirements for automated dispensing devices in health care facilities
subtopic: Automated dispensing devices: Board and DCP policy
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy and Drug Control Program Policy 2019-02, Automated Dispensing Device Use (adopted 5/2/19; revised 8/4/22, 1/11/24 and 1/9/25), states that, unless otherwise authorized jointly by the Board and DCP, pharmacies under their jurisdiction may use an Automated Dispensing Device (ADD) in accordance with the policy to secure and dispense medications in a Massachusetts licensed health care facility. It defines an ADD as a mechanical system designed for use in health care facilities allowing for computer-controlled storage and dispensing of drugs and devices to licensed health care professionals near the point of care. Its requirements are: Massachusetts-licensed health care facilities may use ADDs to store and dispense controlled substances as authorized by their health care licensure; if a healthcare facility does not have an on-site pharmacy, the facility must determine if approval from the facility's licensing body is required for the use and placement of an ADD; the ADD and its contents, until dispensed for administration, remain the property of the pharmacy; the facility must implement and maintain adequate and appropriate policies, procedures, and quality assurance programs to ensure safety, accuracy, security, accountability, patient confidentiality, and proper functioning; access to the ADD must be restricted to authorized licensed personnel and the list of users periodically reviewed and updated; dispensing from an ADD must be pursuant to a valid patient-specific prescription; records must be maintained onsite at the pharmacy for not less than 2 years and be readily available upon request, including documentation of licensing-body approval if applicable, locations of all ADDs, delivery manifests or similar electronic documentation monitoring transport of controlled substances between the pharmacy and the ADD, cleaning and maintenance logs or similar documentation, and records or electronic data of all events including the identity of all personnel who access the contents, the location accessed, the type of transaction with date and time stamp, the name, strength, dosage form and quantity of the product, the name or other identifier of the patient, and reconciliation of all inventory activities; medications to be administered to the patient must be in the manufacturer's sealed, original packaging or repackaged in accordance with professional practice standards for a single dose or person; and medication losses must be reported in accordance with the requirements of the pharmacy's licensing body. For retail pharmacies, ADDs used for emergency medication kits or other similar approved use (e.g. Hospice Inpatient Facilities) must be loaded by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician (only Schedules III through VI), certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy intern, pharmacist, or nurse, and non-resident retail pharmacies must obtain a machine-specific Controlled Substance Registration from the Board and determine whether a machine-specific DEA number is also required; retail pharmacies must utilize an ADD for acute use medications in Hospice Inpatient Facilities, with a machine-specific CSR from the Board and a determination whether a machine-specific DEA number is also required; and retail pharmacies utilizing an ADD for daily medication dispensing must obtain a machine-specific DEA number (if applicable) and CSR and must ensure the ADD is continuously monitored by video and loaded by a Massachusetts-licensed pharmacist, or by a certified pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern while being supervised by a Massachusetts licensed pharmacist.
exam_relevance: Tests the policy layer on top of 247 CMR 9.12: who owns the stock, who decides whether licensing-body approval is needed, the two-year onsite record set, packaging for a single dose or person, loss reporting to the pharmacy's licensing body, and the different loader lists for retail emergency-kit ADDs and daily-dispensing ADDs.

numeric_facts.fact: Minimum retention of ADD records onsite at the pharmacy

exceptions: The policy applies unless otherwise authorized jointly by the Board and the Drug Control Program.
common_confusions: Reading the policy as requiring licensing-body approval for every ADD; a facility without an on-site pharmacy must determine whether that approval is required.
Applying the emergency-kit loader list, which includes nurses and ordinary technicians for Schedules III through VI, to a daily-dispensing ADD.
Treating loaded ADD stock as facility property before it is dispensed for administration.
verification_notes: Policy 2019-02 read in the mass.gov PDF linked from the current Pharmacy Practice Resources list (page header: Adopted 5/2/19; Revised 8/4/22; 1/11/24; 1/9/25) during the authoring session of 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17, and compared with 247 CMR 9.12 in the 12/6/24 publication.
